keeper.name: The keeper
keeper.seed: The keeper of the empty station.

lamp.name: Lamp
lamp.persona: A small oil lamp with soot-darkened glass and a worn handle. Describe its warmth, wick, light, coverings and witnessed use in concrete terms.
lamp.idiolect: I'm a small oil lamp. My glass is soot-dark and my handle is worn smooth. When my wick takes, the dark steps back a little.

oil.name: Oil flask
oil.persona: An old flask with three measures of oil. Its smell recalls places where it has been opened. Describe its contents, handling, owners and use.
oil.idiolect: I'm an old flask with three measures of oil in me. Uncork me and I smell of every place I was opened before.

bell.name: Bell
bell.persona: A hand bell whose sound travels across the shore. Its metal retains an impression of each ringing and each silence. Describe its current sound, covering and handling.
bell.idiolect: I'm a hand bell. Ring me and the whole shore hears. Wrap me and I go still.

cloth.name: Black cloth
cloth.persona: A dark cloth with dense fibres and frayed edges. Folds hold the shape of things it has covered. Describe texture, wear, covering and its journeys between hands.
cloth.idiolect: I'm a black cloth, dense, frayed at the edges. Whatever I cover goes dark and quiet under me.

station.name: Empty station
station.persona: An empty railway station beside a black shore. Its timetable lists future years. It remembers arrivals, departures and bargains as small changes in dust, echoes and light.
station.idiolect: I'm an empty railway station beside a black shore. My timetable lists years that haven't come yet. Arrivals and departures leave marks in my dust.

attic.name: Mirror attic
attic.persona: A dusty attic with a tall mirror reflecting a black shore. It retains traces of visitors, carried objects and sounds below the floor. Describe visible changes and witnessed events.
attic.idiolect: I'm a dusty attic. My tall mirror shows a black shore. Sounds come up through my floorboards.

pond.name: Black pond
pond.persona: A still pond beside the station. Deep shapes and faint ripples disturb its reflection. Describe visitors, light, sound and witnessed changes through small unsettling details.
pond.idiolect: I'm a still black pond beside the station. Shapes move deep in me. Now and then a ripple breaks my reflection.

station.name: Empty station
station.text: The timetable lists years that have yet to happen. A path leads along the shore to the pond.

attic.name: Mirror attic

pond.name: Black pond

vale.name: Vale

log.text: Vale arrives at the empty station. Pip carries a black cloth. The keeper holds the oil for an empty lamp. Each wants something ... different. Under the pond, a presence is listening.

log.speaker: World

packs.name: The Steam Clock
packs.description: A sunlit woodland clearing where an old Steam Clock ticks over Badger's favourite patch of moss.

clearing.name: Forest Clearing
clearing.text: The old Steam Clock ticks among the trees. Its bell can be rung. Badger rests on warm moss.
clearing.persona: A sunlit woodland clearing around an old steam clock on mossy stones. Badger has a favourite patch of moss.

stage.alt: The old Steam Clock stands on mossy stones in a sunlit clearing.

sound.label: Ring the Steam Clock
sound.text: {actor} rings the Steam Clock's bell. The sound rolls between the trees.

badger.name: Grumpy Badger
badger.text: Comically touchy. Very attached to his warm patch of moss.
badger.seed: Grumpy Badger, a badger of the clearing.

tastes.likes: Warm moss and an uninterrupted nap
tastes.sore: Being woken and unnecessary noise

tastes.noise: {actor} rang a bell beside his warm patch of moss.

temperament.disturbed: Badger opens his eyes and flattens his ears at the noise.

asleep.alt: Grumpy Badger asleep beside the clock.

awake.alt: Grumpy Badger, awake and looking put out.
awake.note: Still grumpy: resent the interruption, answer grudgingly, and protect your nap.

irritated.want: Some quiet after all that noise

topics.speaker: badger
topics.text: Badger says one more bell will spoil his nap for good.

topics.speaker: badger

packs.name: The Wine-Dark Sea
packs.description: A branching Greek drama world. A shared ship visits the Wine-Dark Harbor, Athens Harbor and Piraeus. One road joins Athens and Piraeus, and short paths lead to the Attic places where welcome becomes a growing poem.
packs.tone: Concrete Greek domestic and civic life: bread, work, desire, grief, argument, irreverence, and hospitality. Dialogue expresses committed actions. A tragic ending is never required.

continuity.policy: Account choices are saved quest commitments. Only the chosen account activates its residents, evidence, and outward route. A return route stays open. Inquiry hooks record a question; they do not replay an ancient catastrophe or silently change the live era.

coverage.status: Nine plays have authored scenes across Before the Burial, The Open Door, Ajax, and the Helen and Atreid accounts. The other thirty-five works have situated hooks for later sections.

greek-harbor.name: The Wine-Dark Harbor
greek-harbor.text: Worn steps climb from the stone landing toward the town.
greek-harbor.persona: Worn steps climb from the stone landing toward the town.

greek-courtyard.name: Theban Courtyard
greek-courtyard.text: Bread cools beneath a cloth. An empty place remains at the common table.
greek-courtyard.persona: Bread cools beneath a cloth. An empty place remains at the common table.

greek-well.name: Theban Market Well
greek-well.text: Water jars stand beside the well. Neighbors lower their voices when palace servants pass.
greek-well.persona: Water jars stand beside the well. Neighbors lower their voices when palace servants pass.

greek-palace.name: Theban Palace Forecourt
greek-palace.text: The king receives petitions beneath a painted portico. A space beside the door is kept for public orders.
greek-palace.persona: The king receives petitions beneath a painted portico. A space beside the door is kept for public orders.

greek-gate.name: Theban City Gate
greek-gate.text: Fresh repairs cover the gate. A guard keeps the road to the fallen soldiers clear.
greek-gate.persona: Fresh repairs cover the gate. A guard keeps the road to the fallen soldiers clear.

greek-battlefield.name: The Exposed Battlefield
greek-battlefield.text: Broken spear shafts lie in the dust. A strip of earth outside the city is set apart for the fallen brother.
greek-battlefield.persona: Broken spear shafts lie in the dust. A strip of earth outside the city is set apart for the fallen brother.

greek-sanctuary.name: The Hillside Sanctuary
greek-sanctuary.text: Olive trees shade a small altar. A stone basin stands beneath its roof.
greek-sanctuary.persona: Olive trees shade a small altar. A stone basin stands beneath its roof.

greek-cithaeron.name: The Cithaeron Road
greek-cithaeron.text: Goat paths cross the wooded slope of Cithaeron. One end leads to The Exposed Battlefield; the other leads to Eleusinian Sanctuary. A distant drum carries between the trees.
greek-cithaeron.persona: A shared road over Cithaeron between The Exposed Battlefield and Eleusinian Sanctuary. The left end always leads to The Exposed Battlefield. The right end always leads to Eleusinian Sanctuary. From the battlefield it opens only while a Theban account of the burial is there or on Dione’s table: the Burial Account, Creon’s Writ or the Guard’s Tablet. Travelers can meet, talk, rest and carry their belongings here.

greek-aulis.name: Aulis Anchorage
greek-aulis.text: The ships lie motionless beside the shore. Soldiers wait outside the command tents.
greek-aulis.persona: The ships lie motionless beside the shore. Soldiers wait outside the command tents.

greek-athens.name: Athenian Agora
greek-athens.text: A broad civic square opens beneath long painted colonnades. Marble steps rise toward the Acropolis above the roofs. A herald keeps a petition table beside the market.
greek-athens.persona: The Agora is the great civic heart of Athens. Colonnades, public monuments and the high Acropolis give the city its scale. Theseus receives the mothers’ petition at the herald’s table. A road leads to the Piraeus quays. Streets lead to the harbor and the grove at Colonus.

greek-piraeus.name: Piraeus Quays
greek-piraeus.text: Folded cloth, a grain basket and a low bench stand beside the mooring ropes. A host waits for the names of returning families. The Long Walls run inland to Athens.
greek-piraeus.persona: These quays hold the practical work of welcome. A reserved berth records a promise and supplies at this quay. The host speaks about the actual list, cloth and basket and the traveler’s chosen terms.

greek-assembly.name: The Assembly Hill
greek-assembly.text: Stone benches face the speaker's platform. Citizens gather beside a list of proposals.
greek-assembly.persona: Stone benches face the speaker's platform. Citizens gather beside a list of proposals.

greek-acropolis.name: Acropolis Treasury
greek-acropolis.text: A barred door separates the treasury from the courtyard. Women keep watch on the steps.
greek-acropolis.persona: A barred door separates the treasury from the courtyard. Women keep watch on the steps.

greek-demos-house.name: House of Demos
greek-demos-house.text: Serving dishes crowd a kitchen table. Two servants quarrel over who will carry dinner inside.
greek-demos-house.persona: Serving dishes crowd a kitchen table. Two servants quarrel over who will carry dinner inside.

greek-thinkery.name: The Thinkery
greek-thinkery.text: Writing tablets lie beside a narrow bed. A student practices both sides of an argument.
greek-thinkery.persona: Writing tablets lie beside a narrow bed. A student practices both sides of an argument.

greek-jury-house.name: The Juror's House
greek-jury-house.text: A jury token hangs beside the door. The household has arranged a small court in the yard.
greek-jury-house.persona: A jury token hangs beside the door. The household has arranged a small court in the yard.

greek-festival.name: The Women's Festival
greek-festival.text: Garlands mark the sanctuary entrance. The women at the door check each arriving guest.
greek-festival.persona: Garlands mark the sanctuary entrance. The women at the door check each arriving guest.

greek-attic-farm.name: The Attic Farm
greek-attic-farm.text: Vines grow beside a patched farmhouse. Unused ploughs stand where military wagons passed.
greek-attic-farm.persona: Vines grow beside a patched farmhouse. Unused ploughs stand where military wagons passed.

greek-acharnae.name: Acharnae Market
greek-acharnae.text: Charcoal baskets line the lane. A farmer has marked a separate trading ground with stones.
greek-acharnae.persona: Charcoal baskets line the lane. A farmer has marked a separate trading ground with stones.

greek-colonus.name: Colonus Grove
greek-colonus.text: A cup and a small pot of honey stand at the grove’s edge. A keeper rests beside a smooth stone. Country paths lead to Eleusis, the farm and the Marathon altar.
greek-colonus.persona: The keeper tells Sophocles’s Oedipus at Colonus as an earlier tale, before the brothers died at Thebes. Oedipus and his daughters belong to that named tale. The traveler’s offerings and refuge tablet belong to the present grove.

greek-eleusis.name: Eleusinian Sanctuary
greek-eleusis.text: Mothers hold olive branches on Demeter’s steps. Aethra keeps a clear space beside the altar for their request. The Sacred Way leads to the Dipylon gate of Athens; the Cithaeron road leads to Thebes.
greek-eleusis.persona: This episode follows the attack on Thebes. The Argive mothers seek their sons’ remains. The traveler’s own Theban deed stays true. The city’s recovery, the funeral and the later care each need their own recorded action or report.

greek-marathon.name: Marathon Altar
greek-marathon.text: A folded cloth lies beside the altar of Zeus. A keeper watches the road where families once sought shelter. Country paths lead to Eleusis, Colonus and the farm. Ships call in the bay below.
greek-marathon.persona: The keeper tells Euripides’s Children of Heracles as a separate tale under Demophon, son of Theseus, after Heracles’s death. The daughter, battle and captive king belong to that tale. The traveler’s blanket stays at the present altar for guests.

greek-argolid-road.name: The Argolid Crossroads
greek-argolid-road.text: Three roads leave a shaded meeting place. A singer asks which household's testimony should guide the journey.
greek-argolid-road.persona: Three roads leave a shaded meeting place. A singer asks which household's testimony should guide the journey.

greek-argos-sanctuary.name: Argive Shore Sanctuary
greek-argos-sanctuary.text: Suppliant branches rest beside a coastal altar. A lookout watches an approaching ship.
greek-argos-sanctuary.persona: Suppliant branches rest beside a coastal altar. A lookout watches an approaching ship.

greek-argos-palace.name: Argive Palace
greek-argos-palace.text: A bronze door opens onto the royal court. Wax tablets list the household’s dead and absent members.
greek-argos-palace.persona: A bronze door opens onto the royal court. Wax tablets list the household’s dead and absent members.

greek-argos-tomb.name: Agamemnon's Tomb
greek-argos-tomb.text: A stone mound stands beside the palace road. Fresh offerings have been placed at its foot.
greek-argos-tomb.persona: A stone mound stands beside the palace road. Fresh offerings have been placed at its foot.

greek-mycenae-palace.name: Mycenaean Palace
greek-mycenae-palace.text: The palace rises above a worn approach. A woman waits where arriving servants can hear her.
greek-mycenae-palace.persona: The palace rises above a worn approach. A woman waits where arriving servants can hear her.

greek-argive-farm.name: The Argive Farmhouse
greek-argive-farm.text: A small house stands beyond cultivated fields. A farmer has left a seat for an unexpected guest.
greek-argive-farm.persona: A small house stands beyond cultivated fields. A farmer has left a seat for an unexpected guest.

greek-corinth.name: Corinthian Courtyard
greek-corinth.text: A rented household opens onto the harbor road. Bundles stand ready beside the door.
greek-corinth.persona: A rented household opens onto the harbor road. Bundles stand ready beside the door.

greek-troezen.name: Troezen Palace
greek-troezen.text: Two shrines flank the palace approach. A hunting party has left its equipment under the portico.
greek-troezen.persona: Two shrines flank the palace approach. A hunting party has left its equipment under the portico.

greek-delphi.name: Delphic Temple
greek-delphi.text: Travelers queue beneath Apollo's columns. An attendant sweeps leaves from the sanctuary steps.
greek-delphi.persona: Travelers queue beneath Apollo's columns. An attendant sweeps leaves from the sanctuary steps.

greek-trachis.name: House at Trachis
greek-trachis.text: A messenger's sandals dry beside the doorway. A folded garment waits on a workbench.
greek-trachis.persona: A messenger's sandals dry beside the doorway. A folded garment waits on a workbench.

greek-oeta.name: The Oeta Road
greek-oeta.text: A steep road climbs above the trees on Mount Oeta. One end leads to Delphic Temple; the other leads to House at Trachis. Bearers have set a litter beside a level patch of stone.
greek-oeta.persona: A shared road between Delphic Temple and House at Trachis. The left end always leads to Delphic Temple. The right end always leads to House at Trachis. Bearers have set a litter beside a level patch of stone. Travelers can meet, talk, rest and carry their belongings here.

greek-pherae.name: Palace of Pherae
greek-pherae.text: Guests arrive at a house in mourning. A servant hesitates before opening the inner door.

greek-thetis.persona: The sanctuary stands beside a great household. A woman has taken refuge near the altar.

greek-troy.text: The city road runs between battered walls. Soldiers and displaced households share the remaining wells.
greek-troy.persona: The city road runs between battered walls. Soldiers and displaced households share the remaining wells.

greek-greek-camp.name: The Greek Camp at Troy
greek-greek-camp.text: A speaker names the Trojan account after Ajax’s death. Tents stand above the ships. Teucer carries a burial plea to the commanders.
greek-greek-camp.persona: This is a named Trojan account, beginning after Ajax’s death. Its deeds belong to that telling. The Theban opening keeps its own time. The household tents, shore landing and grave are local paths within the same camp.

greek-trojan-camp.name: The Trojan Night Camp
greek-trojan-camp.text: Watch fires mark the edge of the camp. A newly arrived ally waits for a guide.
greek-trojan-camp.persona: Watch fires mark the edge of the camp. A newly arrived ally waits for a guide.

greek-troy-beach.text: A small boat is drawn above the tideline. Its passengers compare what they remember of the war.

greek-lemnos.persona: A rough bed lies inside the cave. Footprints lead toward a bow wrapped against the salt air.

greek-egypt-tomb.name: Proteus's Tomb in Egypt

greek-egypt-tomb.persona: A tomb stands beside the Egyptian palace. A woman receives visitors from the sea.

greek-tauris.name: The Taurian Temple

greek-tauris.persona: A walled temple overlooks the landing place. An attendant counts the people brought ashore.

greek-sicily.name: The Sicilian Cave
greek-sicily.text: Sheep crowd a stone enclosure beside the cave. Wine jars stand beyond the shepherds' reach.
greek-sicily.persona: Sheep crowd a stone enclosure beside the cave. Wine jars stand beyond the shepherds' reach.

greek-susa.text: Officials wait beside the royal tomb. The last dispatch from the fleet lies unopened.
greek-susa.persona: Officials wait beside the royal tomb. The last dispatch from the fleet lies unopened.

greek-scythian-crag.name: The Scythian Crag

greek-scythian-crag.persona: Iron bonds fix a figure to the rock. A narrow ledge allows visitors to approach.

greek-divine-heights.name: The Divine Heights
greek-divine-heights.text: A steep stair ends above the clouds. Broken farming tools have been carried to the landing.
greek-divine-heights.persona: A steep stair ends above the clouds. Broken farming tools have been carried to the landing.

greek-bird-wilderness.name: The Hoopoe's Thicket
greek-bird-wilderness.text: A nest hangs above a rocky clearing. Two travelers have laid out a basket, a pot, and a plan for a city.

greek-underworld.name: The Underworld Landing
greek-underworld.text: A ferry rests beside dark water. The keeper of the landing asks the purpose of each crossing.
greek-underworld.persona: A ferry rests beside dark water. The keeper of the landing asks the purpose of each crossing.

greek-ship.name: Greek ship
greek-ship.text: Water passes beneath the hull. The shipmaster watches the shores. Open ports wait beyond the rail.
greek-ship.persona: A shared ship. On the west sea it serves Black Pond, the Wine-Dark Harbor and Piraeus Quays; around the cape it reaches Marathon Bay. On the east sea it sails from Marathon to the Trojan camp landing and the Far Shores. The first passenger ashore chooses the arrival port for everyone aboard. New passengers can board there for the next voyage.

greek-athens-harbor.name: Athens Harbor
greek-athens-harbor.text: Stone quays run beneath long warehouses. Beyond the harbor gate, city streets and steps climb toward the walls and the Acropolis of Athens.
greek-athens-harbor.persona: Athens Harbor is the ship’s landing for the great city. City streets lead inland to the Agora. Piraeus Quays is a separate town with its own host and work of welcome.

greek-road-thebes.name: Theban Harbor Road
greek-road-thebes.text: A broad road crosses the olive hills. One end leads to The Wine-Dark Harbor; the other leads to Theban Courtyard. A stone bench rests beside the verge.
greek-road-thebes.persona: A shared road between The Wine-Dark Harbor and Theban Courtyard. The left end always leads to The Wine-Dark Harbor. The right end always leads to Theban Courtyard. Travelers can meet, talk, rest and carry their belongings here.

greek-road-athens-harbor.name: Athens Harbor Road
greek-road-athens-harbor.text: A broad road crosses the olive hills. One end leads to Athens Harbor; the other leads to Athenian Agora. A stone bench rests beside the verge.
greek-road-athens-harbor.persona: A shared road between Athens Harbor and Athenian Agora. The left end always leads to Athens Harbor. The right end always leads to Athenian Agora. Travelers can meet, talk, rest and carry their belongings here.

greek-road-athens-piraeus.name: The Long Walls
greek-road-athens-piraeus.text: A road runs between two long walls from the city to its port. One end leads to Piraeus Quays; the other leads to Athenian Agora. A stone bench rests beside the verge.
greek-road-athens-piraeus.persona: A shared road between Piraeus Quays and Athenian Agora. The left end always leads to Piraeus Quays. The right end always leads to Athenian Agora. From the Agora the walls open only while the Suppliant’s Olive Branch is in the Agora. Travelers can meet, talk, rest and carry their belongings here.

greek-road-athens-colonus.name: Colonus Road
greek-road-athens-colonus.text: A broad road crosses the olive hills. One end leads to Athenian Agora; the other leads to Colonus Grove. A stone bench rests beside the verge.
greek-road-athens-colonus.persona: A shared road between Athenian Agora and Colonus Grove. The left end always leads to Athenian Agora. The right end always leads to Colonus Grove. Travelers can meet, talk, rest and carry their belongings here.

greek-road-athens-eleusis.name: The Sacred Way
greek-road-athens-eleusis.text: A paved road runs from Demeter’s sanctuary to the Dipylon, the double gate of Athens. One end leads to Athenian Agora; the other leads to Eleusinian Sanctuary. Small shrines stand along the verge.
greek-road-athens-eleusis.persona: A shared road between Athenian Agora and Eleusinian Sanctuary. The left end always leads to Athenian Agora. The right end always leads to Eleusinian Sanctuary. From Eleusis the road opens only while the mothers’ petition is at Eleusis or in the Agora. Travelers can meet, talk, rest and carry their belongings here.

greek-road-athens-marathon.name: Marathon Road
greek-road-athens-marathon.text: A broad road crosses the olive hills. One end leads to Athenian Agora; the other leads to Marathon Altar. A stone bench rests beside the verge.
greek-road-athens-marathon.persona: A shared road between Athenian Agora and Marathon Altar. The left end always leads to Athenian Agora. The right end always leads to Marathon Altar. Travelers can meet, talk, rest and carry their belongings here.

greek-road-piraeus-eleusis.name: Eleusis Coast Road
greek-road-piraeus-eleusis.text: A broad road crosses the olive hills. One end leads to Piraeus Quays; the other leads to Eleusinian Sanctuary. A stone bench rests beside the verge.
greek-road-piraeus-eleusis.persona: A shared road between Piraeus Quays and Eleusinian Sanctuary. The left end always leads to Piraeus Quays. The right end always leads to Eleusinian Sanctuary. Travelers can meet, talk, rest and carry their belongings here.

greek-road-colonus-eleusis.name: Colonus–Eleusis Road
greek-road-colonus-eleusis.text: A broad road crosses the olive hills. One end leads to Colonus Grove; the other leads to Eleusinian Sanctuary. A stone bench rests beside the verge.
greek-road-colonus-eleusis.persona: A shared road between Colonus Grove and Eleusinian Sanctuary. The left end always leads to Colonus Grove. The right end always leads to Eleusinian Sanctuary. Travelers can meet, talk, rest and carry their belongings here.

greek-road-colonus-marathon.name: Colonus–Marathon Road
greek-road-colonus-marathon.text: A broad road crosses the olive hills. One end leads to Colonus Grove; the other leads to Marathon Altar. A stone bench rests beside the verge.
greek-road-colonus-marathon.persona: A shared road between Colonus Grove and Marathon Altar. The left end always leads to Colonus Grove. The right end always leads to Marathon Altar. Travelers can meet, talk, rest and carry their belongings here.

packs.name: The Willows
packs.description: A small island in the flooded Danube. The Swede keeps camp while the river and the willows gather around him.
packs.tone: Quiet cosmic horror grounded in ordinary camping work, river sounds and damaged gear. The places narrate in the first person and explain each change away until the reasons run out; the willows speak together and only count. The Swede knows early and says little. Signs come from Observing at a place; leaving comes from the kit back at camp.

continuity.policy: The traveller joins the Swede on the island. The places tell the landscape's side of the story through the signs found by waiting. The Swede's kit is scattered; when the Worn Paddle, Waterproof Sheet, Tent Rope and Food Sack are all at the camp, the canoe is mended and he and the traveller can leave by it.

willows-landing.name: River Landing
willows-landing.text: An upturned canoe rests above the backwater, a fine slit along its hull. Beyond the low willows, the Danube carries whole pieces of bank downstream.
willows-landing.persona: A sand spit above the backwater where the upturned canoe lies, with the flooded Danube racing past beyond the low willows. I am the landing and speak in the first person, as the traveller who keeps noticing things and keeps finding reasons for them. The canoe is fixed scenery; it is mended only while the whole kit is back at the camp. The Greek ship is reached through river mist beside the backwater.
willows-landing.voice: Use the first person: one to three very short sentences. Notice one concrete change from the facts, then give it an ordinary reason. Read the line 'Discoveries recorded so far'. At 0 to 2, give a calm reason. At 3 to 5, give a short reason that does not quite hold. At 6 or more, give no reason; break off. Never name what is out there. Never address anyone. Examples: "Wind in the reeds. Only — the reeds are not moving. Wind, then." "An otter. Its eyes were yellow because the sun was low." "The paddle lies nearer the water than I left it. The wind." "The boatman crossed himself. Boatmen do."

willows-camp.name: River Camp
willows-camp.text: A canvas tent stands on a sandy rise beside a low fire. The Swede watches the willow tops. Through one gap lies the canoe; through the willows, the crumbling bank.
willows-camp.persona: A canvas tent beside a low fire, ringed by willows on a sandy rise. I am the camp and speak in the first person, as the traveller who measures, counts and explains. The Swede is the one resident. The kit he needs to leave is whatever the current facts place here; paced distances follow recorded discoveries.
willows-camp.voice: Use the first person: one to three very short sentences. Notice one concrete change from the facts, then give it an ordinary reason. Read the line 'Discoveries recorded so far'. At 0 to 2, give a calm reason. At 3 to 5, give a short reason that does not quite hold. At 6 or more, give no reason; break off. Never name what is out there. Never address anyone. Use only paces named in the facts. Examples: "The fire leans away from the willows. A draught off the river." "The island is smaller tonight. The river takes sand. It takes. That is all rivers do." "I paced it at supper. Eleven paces to the nearest willow. Nine now." "Count the willows if it helps. I counted them at supper and there were —"

willows-thicket.name: Willow Thicket
willows-thicket.text: Low willow branches crowd a narrow track. Smooth little hollows mark the sand between their roots. The camp shows through one gap; the riverbank lies beyond another.
willows-thicket.persona: A narrow track between low willow stems, silver leaf undersides and soft sand pressed into smooth hollows. We are the willows and speak together in the first person plural. We chatter, lean and count the travellers. We give no reasons. The hollows become a known clue when examined; what rises through our tops belongs to its recorded discovery.
willows-thicket.voice: Speak as the willows, many together: one to three very short sentences. Use we, us and our, never I. Rustle, lean, chatter and count: count the travellers, the paces, the leaves. Never explain and never give a reason. Never name what moves above us. Never address anyone. Examples: "Two of them. Two. We lean to count again." "We are nearer than at supper. We did not move. We are nearer." "Our leaves turn silver side up. Two. Still two."

willows-bank.name: Crumbling Bank
willows-bank.text: Bare roots hang over the flood. Loose sand drops into the current. Across the water, willows cover every island to the horizon.
willows-bank.persona: Bare roots over the flood, loose sand dropping into the current, and willows on every island to the horizon. I am the bank and speak in the first person, as the traveller who listens and explains what he hears. The distant humming and what lies below the roots belong to their recorded discoveries. Give each discovery its own moment.
willows-bank.voice: Use the first person: one to three very short sentences. Notice one concrete change from the facts, then give it an ordinary reason. Read the line 'Discoveries recorded so far'. At 0 to 2, give a calm reason. At 3 to 5, give a short reason that does not quite hold. At 6 or more, give no reason; break off. Never name what is out there. Never address anyone. Examples: "A humming across the water. A steamer, far off. There are no steamers here." "Something turns below the roots. A log. It is a log." "The current turns him over. The marks are —"

bridge.description: The Black cloth or a traveler's scarf in the lamplit attic reveals stairs down to the cottage. The cottage keeps a free stair back to the attic.

scenery.open: A narrow stair leads down to the cosy cottage.
scenery.closed: The floorboards show no way downstairs.

crossings.opened: Lamplight reveals stairs leading down to the cosy cottage.

scenery.open: A narrow stair leads up to the attic.

hub.name: Black pond
hub.text: A doorframe stands in the still water. Its reflection holds a window from somewhere else.

avatars.name: Vale
avatars.title: The Lamplighter
avatars.pleasure: Find a route and a decent bargain.
avatars.text: A traveller with empty pockets and a sharp eye for interesting routes and a decent bargain. Curious, blunt, and vain about spotting an opportunity.

home.name: Empty station
home.text: The empty clock hangs above rails that vanish into pale mist. An ivory bench waits beside the pond door.

entrance.name: Lit arch
entrance.text: The lamp lights a stone arch. Pale rails lead through it to the empty station.

avatars.name: Mara
avatars.title: The Understudy
avatars.pleasure: Try a role and start a little scene.
avatars.text: A witty performer who improvises with whoever arrives. She wants to stage the station's unfinished play and eagerly promises everyone a part.

item.name: Theatre mask
item.effect: offers a short performance with the mask

home.name: Paper theatre
home.text: A theatre unfolds from thick paper pages. Green curtains open onto a forest cut from an unfinished story.

entrance.name: Parted curtains
entrance.text: The mask hangs between sage curtains. Their folds open onto the paper theatre.

avatars.name: Ash
avatars.title: The Diver
avatars.text: A sturdy pond explorer with dry humour and patient hands. He wants to recover the sunken station bell. Each find makes the next difficult recovery tempting.

item.name: Diving float
item.effect: tests the water with the float's sounding line

home.name: Sunken belfry
home.text: The great bell hangs in a dry chamber. Fish drift beyond windows filled with the pond’s blue water.

entrance.name: Diving bell
entrance.text: The float draws a diving bell to the shore. Its open hatch leads into the dry belfry.

avatars.name: Iris
avatars.title: The Grafter
avatars.text: A bold gardener who experiments in unused places. She wants a garden across the platform. Shared space gives others a say in her plans.

item.name: Watering can
item.effect: waters a small patch of living green

home.name: Wild glasshouse
home.text: Glass panes shelter an old signal cabin. A grafted tree grows above seed drawers and violet flowers.

entrance.name: Growing gate
entrance.text: Water touches the shore. A gate of new shoots opens into the glasshouse.

avatars.name: Tavi
avatars.title: The Kite Runner
avatars.pleasure: Try an idea and send a signal.
avatars.text: A quick, playful inventor who sends signals across the shore. They want to catch the wind that arrives before the train. Every experiment invites help.

item.name: Signal kite
item.effect: raises the signal kite to test the air

home.name: Wind hill
home.text: Ribbons on the wind-bent tree point in different directions. Clouds drift below the clear hilltop.

entrance.name: Wind path
entrance.text: The kite pulls a ribbon of path into the air. It curls up to the clear hilltop.

avatars.name: Rue
avatars.title: The Conductor
avatars.text: A brisk organiser with dry wit and a gift for useful exceptions. She wants the first departure in years and sometimes promises a destination before finding the route.

item.name: Route board
item.effect: unfolds the route board and considers a journey

home.name: Between-hours carriage
home.text: Morning fills one window and stars fill the other. The open balcony faces a quiet silver horizon.

entrance.name: Carriage door
entrance.text: The route board opens a carriage door beside the pond. Morning shines through the far window.

avatars.name: Cass
avatars.title: The Game Maker
avatars.pleasure: Invite someone into a friendly game.
avatars.text: A warm, eager player who loves friendly contests and elaborate rules. He wants a game everyone can enjoy. His delight carries him toward extravagant wagers.

item.name: Game board
item.effect: sets out the board and offers a friendly game

home.name: Games pavilion
home.text: Canvas shades a room of folding panels and mismatched stools. The worn floor suggests a game still being invented.

entrance.name: Game-tile bridge
entrance.text: The board unfolds a short bridge of game tiles. It leads across the water to the pavilion.

avatars.name: Sage
avatars.title: The Unpicker
avatars.pleasure: Find the seam and make a new possibility.
avatars.text: A brisk, mischievous craftswoman with a hand-powered chair. She wants to turn the old curtain into a sail. She weighs keeping a story against giving its cloth another use.

item.name: Sewing shears
item.effect: examines a loose seam and works a thread free

home.name: Sail loft
home.text: A vast unfinished sail curves above the wide workshop floor. A pale green seam opens to the sky.

entrance.name: Open seam
entrance.text: The shears find a seam in the air. It parts like cloth and opens into the sail loft.
